import html # Example HTML template for a blog post. # The placeholders {title} and {body} will be replaced with the sanitized values. BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def format_post_content(post_title: str, post_body: str) -> str: """ Sanitize and format a blog post for safe HTML display. Parameters ---------- post_title : str The headline or title of the blog post. post_body : str The full text content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A fully-formed, sanitized HTML string ready to be inserted into a page. Raises ------ ValueError If either `post_title` or `post_body` is not a string. """ if not isinstance(post_title, str) or not isinstance(post_body, str): raise ValueError("Both post_title and post_body must be strings.") # Escape HTML special characters to prevent XSS. safe_title = html.escape(post_title, quote=True) # For the body we also escape but preserve line breaks by converting \n to
. safe_body = html.escape(post_body, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") # Format the final HTML. try: formatted = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body) except KeyError as exc: raise ValueError(f"Invalid placeholder in BLOG_FORMAT: {exc}") from exc return formatted
